{{short description|English physicist and author (born 1943)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Colin Pask''' (born 1943)<ref>{{cite web |title=British National Bibliography, Pask, Colin, 1943-, The British Library |url=https://bnb.data.bl.uk/doc/person/PaskColin1943- |website=bnb.data.bl.uk}}</ref> is a British mathematical physicist and [[science journalism|science writer]].

== Life ==

He was born in [[Great Gonerby]], on the outskirts of [[Grantham]] in [[Lincolnshire]], where his father was a dairy farmer.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://research.unsw.edu.au/people/emeritus-professor-colin-pask|title=Emeritus Professor Colin Pask|website=research.unsw.edu.au|language=en|access-date=2019-01-29}}</ref> He was educated at [[King's School, Grantham]] from age 11, and went to [[Queen Mary College, London]] for a degree course in theoretical physics and mathematics.<ref name="unsw">{{cite web |title=Colin Pask |url=https://unsw.adfa.edu.au/colin-pask |website=unsw.adfa.edu.au |language=en}}</ref> He graduated B.Sc. there in 1964.<ref name="JOSA">{{cite book |title=Journal of the Optical Society of America: Optics and image science. A |date=1986 |publisher=The Society |page=1106 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9yUXAQAAMAAJ |language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
Pask studied for a Ph.D. in [[nuclear physics]] under [[John M. Blatt]] at the [[University of New South Wales]] from 1964, graduating in 1967 with a dissertation entitled ''Studies in the Nuclear Three-Body Problem''.<ref name="unsw"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Colin Pask - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=186033 |website=genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref> He spent a period at [[Duke University]], then returned to the University of New South Wales as lecturer in the Department of Applied Mathematics.<ref name="JOSA"/>

In 1971 Pask moved to the [[Australian National University]], with an [[Australian Research Council]] fellowship to work in the Department of Applied Mathematics there. He was made a Fellow in 1973, and Senior Fellow in 1978.<ref name="JOSA"/> He moved in 1986 to become head of University College at [[UNSW Canberra at ADFA]], retiring from that post after 12 years.<ref name="unsw"/>

Pask is now Emeritus Professor of Mathematical Sciences and History at University of New South Wales.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.penguinrandomhouse.ca/authors/178309/colin-pask|title=Colin Pask|website=Penguin Random House Canada|language=English|access-date=2019-01-29}}</ref>

==Research interests==
As a post-doctoral researcher, Pask turned to [[optical physics]] and [[biological vision]], among other topics.<ref name="JOSA"/> In 1973 he published with [[Allan Snyder]] an [[optical waveguide]] explanation of the [[Stiles–Crawford effect]]. Pask and McIntyre reviewed the theory and experimental results in the area, in a survey from 2013.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=McIntyre |first1=P. |last2=Pask |first2=C. |title=The Stiles–Crawford effect: a theoretical revisit |journal=Journal of Modern Optics |date=1 February 2013 |volume=60 |issue=4 |pages=266–283 |doi=10.1080/09500340.2013.770575 |bibcode=2013JMOp...60..266M |s2cid=121098614 |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/09500340.2013.770575 |issn=0950-0340|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Work of Pask and Kevin Barrell from 1980 contributed to the theory of the [[apposition eye]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Stavenga |first1=Doekele G. |last2=Hardie |first2=Roger C. |title=Facets of Vision |date=6 December 2012 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-3-642-74082-4 |page=40 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=C1vmCAAAQBAJ&pg=PA40 |language=en}}</ref>

During the 1970s, Pask also published on attenuation effects in [[optical fibres]]. He collaborated in this area with Adrian Ankiewicz.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Adams |first1=M. J. |title=An Introduction to Optical Waveguides |date=1981 |publisher=Wiley |isbn=978-0-471-27969-3 |page=330 |language=en}}</ref>

== Works ==

Pask has written some works of popularisation:

* ''Math for the Frightened: Facing Scary Symbols and Everything Else That Freaks You Out About Mathematics'' (2011)<ref>{{cite book |last1=Pask |first1=Colin |title=Math for the Frightened: Facing Scary Symbols and Everything Else that Freaks You Out about Mathematics |date=2011 |publisher=Prometheus Books |isbn=978-1-61614-421-0 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zP4ikgAACAAJ |language=en}}</ref>
* ''Magnificent Principia: Exploring Isaac Newton's Masterpiece'' (2013)<ref>{{cite book |last1=Pask |first1=Colin |title=Magnificent Principia: Exploring Isaac Newton's Masterpiece |date=3 September 2013 |publisher=Prometheus Books |isbn=978-1-61614-746-4 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lRhnAAAAQBAJ |language=en}}</ref>
* ''Great Calculations: A Surprising Look Behind 50 Scientific Inquiries'' (2015)<ref>{{cite book |last1=Pask |first1=Colin |title=Great Calculations: A Surprising Look Behind 50 Scientific Inquiries |date=7 July 2015 |publisher=Prometheus Books |isbn=978-1-63388-029-0 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fvjIBAAAQBAJ |language=en}}</ref>
